testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum safe air loss rate for a double combination vehicle?
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than 3 psi in one minute during a static leakage test. Faster air loss means something needs repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have ____ warning lights to show when the ABS is not working.
questions.explanation: ABS vehicles have yellow warning lights to alert drivers when the braking system is not working properly. Learn where this light is located on your vehicle before you drive.

questions.question: Using the brakes creates heat. If too much heat builds up:

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual.

questions.explanation: Brakes can handle a lot of heat, but do not depend only on brakes to slow your vehicle. If brakes get too hot, they may fade and lose stopping power. Also use engine braking.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be placed between an air compressor and the first main reservoir. It prevents air from escaping the system if the compressor develops a leak.

questions.question: Which item is NOT part of a vehicle's air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems include: air compressor, governor, storage tanks, tank drains, alcohol evaporator, safety valve, brake pedal, foundation brakes, supply and application pressure gauges, low air pressure warning signals, stop light switch, spring brakes, and parking brake controls.

questions.question: You must have an air brake endorsement to:

options.text: Operate a vehicle with air brakes.
Drive any truck with a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Operate a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You must pass an air brakes knowledge test to get a license to drive any vehicle with air brakes, including air over hydraulic braking systems.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Help remove water and oil from the air tanks.
Are used to send air to the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air usually contains water and oil that can damage the air brake system if they build up. Air tanks have drain valves to remove this water and oil.

questions.question: A visual low pressure warning signal should activate before air pressure drops to between ____ psi.
questions.explanation: A visual low pressure warning signal should turn on before air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi. This signal can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: Air tank drains should be used to:

options.text: Only be used when it is wet outside.

questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from air tanks. When you use a drain, make sure to drain the tank all the way.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, the rods move the slack adjusters when air pressure enters the brake chambers. Air enters when the driver:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes the rods out and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal:

options.text: Is not required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal. If this signal sounds while driving, stop the vehicle right away and have the system repaired.

questions.question: Brake fade happens when:

options.text: The brakes are used too much.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes are used too much.
questions.explanation: When brakes are used too much, they get very hot. This heat causes them to fade and work less effectively at slowing the vehicle.

questions.question: The air compressor is connected to the:
questions.explanation: The air compressor connects to the engine using gears or a belt. It can be air-cooled or cooled by the engine's cooling system.

questions.question: In cold weather, check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator:
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from building up in the air brake system. In cold weather, check it and refill it every day.

questions.question: During inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should move no more than:
questions.explanation: Park on level ground, set wheel chocks, and disengage the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to check that it moves no more than about one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment by a mechanic.

questions.question: A dual air brake system:

options.text: Has two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
Is one air brake system with two different sets of controls.
Has one system for the left side of the truck and one for the right side, each with separate controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. One system usually controls the rear axle brakes and the other controls the front axle brakes.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems share one air compressor. If the compressor breaks, neither system will work properly.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve releases air:

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if pressure gets too high. If this happens, something in the system is wrong and a mechanic should check it.

questions.question: Emergency brakes:

options.text: Are not required on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have both emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, make sure the ____ turn on automatically when air pressure drops below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check that spring brakes turn on automatically when tank pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Chock the wheels and release air by pressing and releasing the brake pedal. The parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should engage when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake in a newer vehicle?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake uses a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob outward to apply the parking brakes. Push the knob inward to release them.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake, the parking brake, and the emergency brake. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: Water and compressor oil build up in air brake systems. What should be done with them?

options.text: They are needed for the system to work properly.
They should make up about 10 percent of the tank.

questions.explanation: Water and compressor oil can damage the air brake system if they build up. Air storage tanks have drains to remove this buildup. You should drain the tanks manually at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: What is often found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. Water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Tanks must be drained regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using the brake pedal can damage the brakes by combining spring force and air pressure.
